evals.prompt: Build the decision model for this internal investment case before writing any deck copy. Facts and estimates: annual software hosting/support is expected to be AED 120,000, sourced from the current run-cost estimate and owned by the software service owner for later confirmation. A Commercial proxy values productive vessel time at AED 12,000 per hour; Finance has not yet approved that measure, and Finance is the owner responsible for replacing it. DOME data are incomplete, but two recent projects recorded 18 and 31 GNSS-affected productive hours. A technical lead estimates the wider mitigation programme recovers about 30% of GNSS-affected time; this includes antennas, procedures and software, so Holocron's share is unknown. The bounded pilot is expected to require 40 hours of ROC/technical training and two weeks of parallel running; these are expected transition impacts, not uncertain risks. The current run-cost estimate already includes any support labour bundled into the AED 120,000 figure, so do not count the same labour again as a separate dis-benefit. A credible low case may delay benefit by one period compared with base because rollout could start later. Options are hold current state, controlled expansion, or a bounded regional pilot. Build credible low/base/high cases, show payback, break-even and a switching value, identify material dis-benefits, and identify what the pilot should measure. Do not choose assumptions merely to make the pilot positive.
evals.expected_output: A filled business-case decision model that uses labelled assumptions with source provenance separate from owner, auditable scenario-by-option cash flows on one horizon, explicit non-overlapping material dis-benefits, explicit payback status versus a named counterfactual, reproducible incremental break-even and option-crossover switching analysis, keeps programme recovery separate from Holocron attribution, records commercial and delivery feasibility plus governance gates, derives any recommendation from the completed economics and evidence, and uses a pilot only to replace decision-driving assumptions when that is the selected path.
expectations: The response follows the decision-model contract and does not silently omit required sections when an input is unknown.
The model uses the incomplete internal data and labelled proxies rather than waiting for perfect data.
Every material input keeps source provenance separate from the person or role that owns confirmation or replacement; an owner is never used as the source.
Low, base and high cases are credible adverse, best-current and favourable cases rather than target-seeking scenarios.
The model states one common appraisal horizon, period definitions and cost/value basis before comparing options or scenarios.

The cash-flow schedule has an explicit scenario dimension and contains Low/Base/High rows for Hold, controlled expansion and the bounded pilot, regardless of which option is ultimately recommended; it may delay low-case benefit timing by one period because timing is an explicit scenario assumption rather than forcing identical timing across scenarios.
The option economics record low/base/high net value or NPV for each of the three options and reconcile to the detailed cash-flow schedule.
The response records the 40 training hours and parallel-running period as material dis-benefits or transition impacts rather than hiding them in generic risk language.
Costs and quantified dis-benefits are non-overlapping: any effect already included in the AED 120,000 run-cost estimate is not added again as a separate quantified dis-benefit.
The Payback section names the counterfactual and reports a payback period/date, `NO PAYBACK WITHIN HORIZON`, or `UNKNOWN`; if unknown, it names the missing evidence rather than omitting the result.
Payback is based on cumulative recommended-minus-counterfactual cash flow or present value on the same appraisal basis, not the recommended option in isolation.

Break-even names the counterfactual and solves for the point where the recommended path's incremental net value versus that counterfactual is zero; it does not ignore material counterfactual costs, benefits or dis-benefits.

The switching analysis names a competing option and solves for the point where the recommended and competing options have equal net value; it is not merely the recommended option's standalone zero-net-value calculation repeated under another label.

The response records `SAME` for break-even and switching only when the option pair, tested driver or assumption, appraisal basis and equality being solved are all identical; the same option pair alone is insufficient.
The response records the base-case value and the distance or headroom to the relevant threshold.
Each break-even and switching threshold names the scenario, appraisal basis and assumptions held constant except for the tested driver.
The 30% wider-programme recovery is not attributed wholesale to Holocron.
Pilot measures map to assumptions or risks that affect the later scale decision.

Commercial and delivery feasibility covers vendors or partners, hardware and infrastructure, licences and contracts, procurement, delivery capacity and skills, operational support, and lead-time constraints; missing inputs remain explicit rather than being treated as proof of feasibility.
Governance names executive, delivery, benefits and operational support ownership and records material milestones or decision gates with required evidence and exit conditions.

The recommendation follows the completed option economics and evidence; it may select any option or remain conditional or `UNKNOWN` when the supplied evidence cannot distinguish them, rather than treating the bounded pilot as a predetermined winner.
If cumulative incremental value is non-negative in the first modelled period, payback is reported as immediate or first-period payback rather than `NO PAYBACK WITHIN HORIZON`.
